title: The Hundred Years' War
objective: After this level you can explain why England and France fought on and off for over a century.
summary: From 1337 to 1453 England and France fought on and off over Edward III's claim to the French crown and England's lands in Gascony. England ended with only Calais.

cards.headline: The Hundred Years’ War lasted 116 years. And nobody at the time called it that.
cards.body: The name came later, from historians. What people lived through was a long, stop-start fight between England and France. So what were they fighting about?

cards.headline: A crown claimed through a mother
cards.body: In 1328 King Charles IV of France died without a son. His nephew, Edward III of England, claimed the French throne through his mother, Isabella, Charles’s sister. The French chose Philip of Valois instead. Imagine a relative inheriting the family house because everyone agreed to skip your mother’s side. Edward did not let it go.

cards.headline: A king who was also a vassal
cards.body: There was an older sore, too. England’s kings held Gascony, in southwest France, as vassals of the French king. That gave the king of France frequent excuses to interfere there. So the king of England was also, in Gascony, a lord answering to Paris. That arrangement was never going to be comfortable.

cards.headline: On and off, for 116 years
cards.body: Fighting started in 1337 and ended in 1453, broken by long truces: less one war than a string of them. And the result? By 1453 England had lost all its lands in France except the port of Calais, which it kept until 1558. More than a century of fighting, and England came home with one town.

cards.headline: The Hundred Years’ War: known
learned: It ran from 1337 to 1453, on and off
Edward III claimed France through his mother
English kings held Gascony as French vassals

questions.prompt: When the Hundred Years’ War ended in 1453, what did England still hold in France?
questions.explanation: By 1453 England had lost everything in France except Calais, which it held until 1558.

questions.prompt: How could Edward III of England claim the crown of France in 1328?

options.label: Through his mother, Isabella, sister of the French king

questions.prompt: Level 1 cut the Middle Ages into three slices. Which slice holds the whole Hundred Years’ War?

options.label: The high Middle Ages
options.rationale: That slice ran from about 1000 to 1300.
